GBL Platform – Field Staff User Guide

Generating Better Livelihoods Programme  |  Republic of South Africa

For: Linkage Champions (LC) & Linkage Facilitators (LF)  |  Version 1.0  |  March 2026

1. Logging In

The GBL Platform is accessed through a web browser on your phone, tablet, or computer. You need an internet connection and your login credentials from your supervisor.

Login screen — enter your email and password, then tap Login as LC / LF

How to Log In

  1. Open a web browser (Chrome recommended) and go to brac-qa.tekdinext.com
  2. Enter your Username / Email — your work email (e.g. yourname@dsd.gov.za)
  3. Enter your Password — provided by your supervisor
  4. Tap the Login as LC / LF button
  5. You will be taken to the Welcome dashboard
Never share your password. Each login is recorded under your name. If you forget your password, contact your supervisor to reset it.
FieldWhat to EnterExample
Username / EmailYour full work email addressgoldenr@dsd.gov.za
PasswordYour account password (case-sensitive)—
Bookmark the GBL website on your phone. On Android Chrome, tap the menu (3 dots) → "Add to Home screen" for quick access in the field.

2. Dashboard & Home Screen

After logging in, you land on the Welcome screen. This is your starting point for all daily activities.

Home screen after login — three module cards

What You See

Card / ElementWhat It Does
My ParticipantsOpens your full participant caseload list — use this every day
Dashboard (Coming Soon)Will show summary statistics of your caseload progress
My Learning Progress (Coming Soon)Will provide access to training materials and professional development
Hamburger menu (≡ top left)Opens navigation: Home, My Profile, Logout
Golden avatar (top left)Shows your name and current participant context
Tap My Participants to start your day. All your daily tasks — logging visits, updating profiles, recording check-ins — flow from there.

3. Your Profile

Your profile shows your personal information and role within the GBL programme.

My Profile modal — personal details and role

How to View Your Profile

  1. Tap the ≡ hamburger menu (three lines, top-left)
  2. Select My Profile
  3. A panel opens showing your details
  4. To close, tap the × button top-right of the panel
FieldDescription
Full NameYour registered name in the system
LC IDYour unique Linkage Champion identifier (e.g. 3294) — used in reports
Email AddressYour login email address
Phone NumberContact number on file
Service AreaYour assigned site (e.g. Randfontein)
Start DateDate you joined the programme
Language PreferenceLanguage the platform displays in (English default)

Logging Out

  1. Tap the ≡ hamburger menu (top-left)
  2. Tap Logout
  3. You will return to the Login screen
Always log out when leaving a shared device to protect participant data privacy.

4. Participants List

The Participants screen lists all the young women enrolled under your care. From here you can search, filter, log visits, and open individual profiles.

Home → My Participants

The "Not Onboarded" tab shows participants who still need their Household Profile completed. Check this tab daily to track who needs follow-up visits.

5. Adding a New Participant (Onboarding)

Enrolling a new participant takes you through a 3-step process. The steps are: Upload Consent Form → Complete Household Profile → Upload SLA. All three must be completed for full onboarding.

My Participants → [Participant Name] → Enroll Participant
Before enrolling a participant, confirm she is: (1) between 18–35 years old, (2) a South African social grant recipient, and (3) willing to give informed consent.

Step 1 – Personal Information

Last NameReqParticipant's legal surnameAs on ID document
Date of BirthReqDD/MM/YYYYMust be 18–35 years old
ID NumberReq13-digit South African IDSystem validates the format
GenderReqSelect from dropdownGBL targets female participants
Phone NumberReq10-digit mobile numbere.g. 0821234567
Alternative PhoneOptHousehold member's numberFor when participant can't be reached
Home LanguageReqSelect from listZulu, Xhosa, Sotho, etc.
NationalityReqSouth African / Other 

Step 2 – Address / Location

ProvinceReqSelect from dropdowne.g. Gauteng

Step 3 – Benefits Information

FieldReq?What to Enter
Grant Type(s)ReqSelect all grants she receives (Child Support, Disability, etc.). Multiple allowed.
Number of DependantsReqTotal number of people the participant supports

Step 4 – Upload Consent & SLA

After capturing personal information, two documents must be uploaded to complete onboarding:

DocumentWhat It IsHow to Get It
Consent FormSigned form confirming the participant agrees to join the GBL programmeDownload from participant page → print → have participant sign → photograph and upload
SLA (Service Level Agreement)Agreement on what the programme will provide and what the participant commits toSame process — download, sign, upload
Never upload a consent form unless the participant has actually signed it. Uploading without real consent is a programme violation.

6. Participant Detail Page

Clicking a participant's name opens their profile — the hub for all activities.

My Participants → [Participant Name]
Participant detail page — onboarding steps and action buttons

What You Can Do from This Page

ActionPurpose
View ProfileSee the participant's full personal details
Enroll ParticipantStart the onboarding process for a new participant

Download SLA FormDownload the SLA PDF to print and get signed

Onboarding Progress Tracker

At the top of the participant page, a progress indicator shows how many of the 3 onboarding steps are complete (0 of 3 Steps Complete, 1 of 3, etc.).

Complete all 3 onboarding steps within the first two weeks. The Household Profile takes the most time — plan an extra 30–45 minutes at the first visit to complete it.

7. Household Profile

The Household Profile is a comprehensive assessment of the participant's situation, divided into 6 tabs. Complete each tab carefully — this data drives the services the programme links her to.

Participant Page → Complete Household Profile
Complete the Household Profile as a conversation, not an interrogation. Explain why you are asking and how it helps the programme support her.

Saving the Household Profile

  1. Fill in the fields on each tab
  2. Tap Save (or Save Progress) on each tab before moving to the next
  3. You can return and update any tab at a later visit
  4. When all required fields across all 6 tabs are saved, the Household Profile step is marked complete
If a participant can't answer some questions during the first visit, save what you have and complete the rest at the next visit. Partial saves are supported.

8. Log a Visit

Every time you meet with a participant one-on-one, you must log it. Visits are the primary record of your coaching activity and are reviewed by your supervisor.

My Participants → Log Visit button (next to participant name)
Log Visit modal — record a one-on-one coaching visit with date and notes

How to Log a Visit

  1. Find the participant in your list
  2. Tap the Log Visit button on their row
  3. Enter the Visit Date and your Notes
  4. Tap Submit to save, or Save Progress to save a draft
  5. The visit is recorded in the participant's activity history
FieldReq?What to EnterNotes
Visit DateOptDate the visit took place (DD/MM/YYYY)Leave blank for today, or enter a past date
NotesReqFree text — what you discussed, actions taken, participant's situationSupervisors read these notes
Log visits on the day they happen. If you were offline, record details in your field notebook and log as soon as you have data. Use the Visit Date field to enter the actual date.
Good notes example: "Discussed budgeting. Participant opened a savings account last week. Next visit: review her first month savings. Plans to use SRD grant for school fees."

9. Group Check-Ins

Group Check-Ins record attendance and details of group coaching sessions, community events, or group meetings with multiple participants.

My Participants → Group Check-ins button (top right)
Group Check-In form — venue, topic, date, and attendance tracking

How to Record a Group Check-In

  1. From the Participants list, tap the Group Check-ins button (top right)
  2. Fill in the session details (venue, topic, date)
  3. Scroll down to the Attendance section and mark who attended
  4. Tap Submit
FieldReq?What to Enter
VenueReqWhere the session was held (e.g. Community Hall, Randfontein)
TopicReqSelect from dropdown: Financial Management, Life Skills, Job Readiness, Health, etc.
Topic DetailsOptAdditional details about what was covered
DateReqDate the group session took place
AttendanceReqMark each participant who attended from your caseload
Record group attendance even if participants arrived late or left early — it still counts. Note any participants who had to leave early in the Topic Details field.

10. Viewing the Activity Log

The activity history for each participant shows all visits, group check-ins, and contacts ever recorded for them.

How to View

  1. Open a participant's profile page
  2. Scroll down or look for the Activity / Log History section
  3. Each entry shows: date, type, notes, and who logged it

Editing a Log Entry

  1. Find the entry you need to correct
  2. Tap the Edit (pencil) icon on that entry
  3. Make your corrections and tap Save
Only edit entries to correct factual errors (wrong date, typo). Do not delete or alter records to change programme statistics. Your supervisor can see edit history.

11. Marking a Participant as Dropout

If a participant can no longer continue in the programme, you must record this in the system.

Only mark a participant as dropout after at least 3 unsuccessful contact attempts AND with your supervisor's knowledge. Do not mark as dropout for missing one session.

How to Mark a Dropout

  1. Open the participant's profile page
  2. Look for the ⋮ (more) menu or a Status section
  3. Select Mark as Dropout
  4. Select the Reason for Dropout from the list
  5. Enter the Last Contact Date
  6. Add notes explaining the circumstances
  7. Tap Confirm
Dropout ReasonWhen to Use
Moved awayParticipant has relocated outside the service area
Unable to contact3+ attempts with no response
Voluntarily withdrewParticipant explicitly said she does not want to continue
Programme ineligibleFound not to meet eligibility criteria after enrolment
DeceasedParticipant has passed away — handle sensitively
Completed programmeAll milestones achieved — participant has graduated
OtherExplain fully in the notes field

12. Field Tips & Troubleshooting

Working Offline

The GBL Platform requires an internet connection. If you have no signal: write visit details in your field notebook → log them the moment you have data. Use the Visit Date field to enter the actual visit date, not today.

Common Problems & Solutions

ProblemWhat to Do
Page won't load / endless spinnerCheck data connection. Pull down to refresh. Close and reopen the browser app.
Form won't saveLook for red asterisks (*) on required fields — all must be filled before saving.
Can't find a participantUse the Search bar. Check the status tab filter — she may be under "Onboarded" or "Completed" instead of the current tab.
Logged out automaticallyThe system logs out after inactivity. Log in again — your data is not lost.
Logged visit on wrong participantOpen the wrong participant's activity log → find the entry → tap Edit → correct or note the error. Contact supervisor if needed.
Upload button not workingCheck file size (photos should be under 5MB). Try again on WiFi if mobile data is slow.
Session expired messageLog in again. If it keeps happening, clear your browser cache (Chrome menu → Settings → Privacy → Clear browsing data).

Data Quality Rules

  • Log visits on the day they happen — not at end of week
  • Update the Household Profile whenever the participant's situation changes
  • Use the Notes field — supervisors read these to understand context
  • Never enter data for a participant without actually making contact
  • If unsure about a field, ask your supervisor rather than guessing

Getting Help

Problem TypeWho to Contact
Can't log in / forgotten passwordYour supervisor or programme IT support
Participant missing from your listYour supervisor (they manage assignments)
System bug or error messageScreenshot the error with date/time and send to IT support
Guidance on recording a specific situationYour Linkage Facilitator or programme manager
